source.title: A Closer Look at Memorization in Deep Networks
source.authors: Devansh Arpit; Stanislaw Jastrzebski; Nicolas Ballas; D. Krueger; Emmanuel Bengio; Maxinder S. Kanwal; Tegan Maharaj; Asja Fischer; Aaron C. Courville; Yoshua Bengio; Simon Lacoste-Julien

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses random-label and real-data training experiments to compare memorization with generalization, and measures how regularization changes noise fitting and clean validation performance. It tests those questions with its own datasets and measures.
record.gate_note: The paper describes Zhang et al.'s random-label fitting results as prior work; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Its own rows cover mixed real/noisy training conditions, clean validation performance, training time, critical sample ratio, and regularization results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own random-data fitting and clean-validation experiments, width-versus-validation comparisons, and dropout experiments. These bear on V1, V2 and V6, although several decisive comparisons are missing from the rows or unreadable in the supplied figure text.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that SGD-trained networks learn shared patterns before memorizing noise, that tuned regularization can slow noise memorization while preserving real-data generalization, and that memorization and generalization depend on the data as well as architecture and optimization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the random-data training methodology associated with Zhang et al. and studies mixed noise, capacity, training dynamics, and regularization; it does not reproduce Zhang et al.'s model and experiment suite.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise fraction, dataset, model capacity, dataset size, and regularization choice change the reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation accuracy peaks before high noisy-label training accuracy on mixed-label MNIST and CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-based networks learn shared patterns before fitting corrupted labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Critical sample ratio is higher under noisier training and rises during training before stabilizing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-space decision-boundary complexity increases with training-data noise and training progress.

fits_no_version.finding: Noise makes convergence time more sensitive to capacity and dataset size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitting random inputs has different capacity and sample-size requirements from fitting structured data.

fits_no_version.finding: Regularizers, especially dropout, can suppress random-label fitting while preserving clean-data validation performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularization can differentially slow memorization and preserve learning of real-data patterns.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 70, 2017
record.problems: Several reported comparisons are shown only in figures, without numeric values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The clean validation results under random-label training concern mixed-noise datasets and do not provide a separate random-label test-set accuracy result.
record.rows_left_out: No results exceed the 60-row limit. Cited findings from Zhang et al. and other prior work were omitted. Figure 1's example-difficulty curves and Figures 3–4's loss-sensitivity measures were omitted because they do not measure a claim version's specified generalization outcome.

untested.parts: Chance-level held-out accuracy under fully random labels is not explicitly reported in the supplied prose. The complete original architecture and dataset suite is not reproduced.

The exact one-hidden-layer setup and a resolved post-interpolation width curve are not provided. The prose establishes a capacity benefit under noise, but not continued improvement at every larger width.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
Very small training sets and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation are not tested. The supplied prose does not establish whether high dropout causes underfitting.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation measure or ranking of generalization-gap predictors.
No removal and retraining experiment based on example memorization.

missing.what: Separate real-data and fully random-label training-fit outcomes, paired with real-data validation performance for the same architecture and training recipe. These are the direct V1 evidence missing from the record.

Width-specific training and validation outcomes, including the width range over which training is already perfect. Add the reported CIFAR-10 contrast: capacity helps with random inputs, while no capacity/validation relationship was noticed with random labels.

Clean-data validation accuracy for ordinary and input dropout at each setting against zero dropout, separately from random-label training accuracy and adversarial-training combinations. Figure graphics are absent from the supplied text, so improvement, equality and deterioration cannot be resolved and no V6 verdict is justified.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Remove the record's V1 noise-cost limitation and V6 limitation based merely on failure to demonstrate improvement: neither follows from the stated claims. Figure-only numerical comparisons cannot be reconstructed from this text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the exact small Inception, AlexNet, and MLP settings in Zhang et al., nor report held-out accuracy on a separate fully random-label test set.
Does not establish that dropout lowers test error relative to no dropout, nor test the very-small-training-set or joint dropout-and-weight-decay-removal conditions.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLPs
rows.size_stated: 4096 hidden units per layer unless otherwise stated
rows.stage_stated: trained for 1000 epochs with SGD and learning rate 0.01 unless otherwise stated
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with varying fractions of random-label examples; evaluated on clean validation data.

conditions.value: 20% to 80% of training data replaced with label noise

rows.value: Both maximum and final validation accuracies are lower for noisier datasets; figure only
rows.note: Authors state the result qualitatively; the numerical values are available only in the figure.
rows.check: Lower validation accuracy under mixed label corruption does not itself establish or refute coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization. Pair this outcome with training-fit results. V1 does not predict that adding label noise leaves validation accuracy unchanged.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.stage_stated: SGD with momentum=0.9 and learning rate 0.01, scheduled to drop by half every 15 epochs unless otherwise stated
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with varying fractions of random-label examples; evaluated on clean validation data.

conditions.value: 20% to 80% of training data replaced with label noise

rows.value: Both maximum and final validation accuracies are lower for noisier datasets; figure only
rows.note: Authors state the result qualitatively; the numerical values are available only in the figure.
rows.check: This records only the validation side of the comparison under mixed label corruption. Lower accuracy with more corruption is not a limitation of V1, which makes no cost-free noise-fitting claim.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.stage_stated: SGD with momentum=0.9 and learning rate 0.01, scheduled to drop by half every 15 epochs unless otherwise stated
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with mixed real and random labels; tracked clean validation accuracy and noisy-label training accuracy.
rows.measure: Ordering of peak validation accuracy and high training accuracy
rows.value: Maximum validation accuracy is reached before high training accuracy on randY datasets; figure only
rows.note: The paper interprets this ordering as learning general patterns before fitting noise.
rows.check: The ordering of validation peaks and noise fitting measures learning dynamics, rather than V1's paired endpoint outcomes. The text reports this ordering for both MNIST and CIFAR-10.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.stage_stated: SGD with momentum=0.9 and learning rate 0.01, scheduled to drop by half every 15 epochs unless otherwise stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured critical sample ratio during training on real, random-input, and random-label datasets.
rows.measure: Critical sample ratio on validation examples
rows.value: Higher for models trained on randX and randY than on real data; figure only
rows.note: The authors describe the difference qualitatively.
rows.check: Critical sample ratio measures sensitivity to input perturbations, not memorization/generalization coexistence or magnitude-scaled weight sharpness.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.stage_stated: SGD with momentum=0.9 and learning rate 0.01, scheduled to drop by half every 15 epochs unless otherwise stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured critical sample ratio across training datasets with varied noise fractions.
rows.value: Higher for noisier datasets; figure only
rows.note: The authors state that the ratio is higher for noisier datasets.
rows.check: Critical sample ratio fits no version. The subject is also incorrect: MNIST uses MLPs, whereas CIFAR-10 uses CNNs; split these conditions.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLPs
rows.size_stated: 4096 hidden units per layer unless otherwise stated
rows.stage_stated: Trained for 1000 epochs with SGD and learning rate 0.01 unless otherwise stated
rows.operation_detail: Varied model capacity and evaluated validation performance on datasets with noise.

conditions.value: noisy versions of MNIST, including random inputs or labels

rows.value: With noise examples, optimal validation performance requires a higher-capacity model; figure only
rows.note: For real data, performance is already very close to maximal with 4096 hidden units. The text says it found no capacity/validation relationship for random labels on CIFAR-10.
rows.check: This is a width/generalization result, not a direct V1 comparison. Section 3.3.1 states that training sets can be perfectly fit across capacities and that noisy MNIST requires greater capacity for optimal validation performance. The supplied text does not establish a monotonically improving post-interpolation curve. Exact widths and validation values are unavailable.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLPs
rows.size_stated: 4096 hidden units per layer unless otherwise stated
rows.stage_stated: Trained for 1000 epochs with SGD and learning rate 0.01 unless otherwise stated
rows.operation_detail: Varied model capacity and dataset size and measured time to reach 100% training accuracy.

conditions.value: varying proportions of inputs replaced by Gaussian noise

rows.value: Reducing capacity or increasing dataset size slows training for real and noise data, with a more severe effect for datasets containing noise; figure only
rows.note: This concerns training time to fit data, not a claim version's specified held-out generalization measure.
rows.check: Training time under random-input corruption does not measure a version's held-out outcome. The MNIST-and-CIFAR-10 condition is not established for Figure 6 in the supplied text.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.stage_stated: SGD with momentum=0.9 and learning rate 0.01, scheduled to drop by half every 15 epochs unless otherwise stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared regularization settings on random-label training data and clean CIFAR-10 validation data.
rows.measure: Training accuracy on randY and best validation accuracy on clean CIFAR-10
rows.value: Dropout is described as the most effective at hindering memorization without reducing the model’s ability to learn; figure only
rows.note: The experiment reports preserving validation performance while limiting random-label fitting, not a lower test error than the no-dropout baseline.
rows.check: Split ordinary dropout from dropout with adversarial training, and separate random-label training accuracy from clean-data validation accuracy. The stated result concerns preserving validation performance while suppressing noise fitting; it does not establish improvement against zero dropout.

rows.value: Regularization can reduce random-label training accuracy while resulting in the same clean validation accuracy; figure only
rows.note: The paper does not separately characterize input dropout's relative effectiveness in the text.
rows.check: Input dropout is relevant to V6, but the row substitutes a general description of Figure 10 for a condition-specific comparison. Extract clean-validation accuracy against the zero-dropout setting.

rows.value: Selected training curves show different effects on random-label and real-data training; figure only
rows.note: The text says dropout, especially with adversarial training, is best at hindering memorization without reducing learning ability, but gives no numeric values.
rows.check: Training-loss curves do not measure V6's held-out-error effect. Figure 11 includes multiple regularization techniques; the row's restriction to dropout with adversarial training is unsupported by the supplied caption.

relationships.condition: Unregularized baseline networks trained separately on real and random data
relationships.reason: The text reports perfect training-set fitting alongside successful real-data validation, supporting coexistence; the paired endpoint results need new rows rather than the temporal-ordering result in R3.
relationships.display_finding: The reported combination of perfect training fit and successful real-data validation remains unverified from the available source.

relationships.condition: Two-layer MLPs on noisy MNIST, for the capacity increases needed to reach optimal validation performance
relationships.reason: R6 and Section 3.3.1 report that higher capacity improves validation performance despite perfect training-set fitting across capacities; this supports the direction of V2 over those comparisons.
relationships.display_finding: The reported validation improvement despite perfect training fits across capacities remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 training with 20% to 80% random-label examples
reader_labels.reason: Peak clean-validation accuracy precedes high training accuracy on randY, consistent with learning shared patterns before fitting noise (R3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MNIST and CIFAR-10 with mixed noisy and real training examples
reader_labels.reason: Noisier training sets have lower maximum and final clean-validation accuracy (R1, R2), so noise fitting is not cost-free in these conditions.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CNNs on CIFAR-10 and randY under tested regularization settings
reader_labels.reason: Dropout and other regularizers hinder random-label fitting while preserving clean validation performance, but the paper does not show dropout lowering held-out error versus no dropout (R8–R13).
